newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bouygues Offshore wins $65 mln contract.
newsitem.headline: Bouygues Offshore wins $65 mln contract.

text.p: Bouygues Offshore, a unit of construction group Bouygues, said on Friday it had obtained a $65 million share of a contract to double the size of the Sheskharis oil terminal on the Russian Black Sea.

The contract was signed by Bouygues Offshore and JSC Onako Terminal, a subsidiary of the Russian group Onako. "The works entrusted to Bouygues Offshore are worth approximately $65 million and expected to last 17 months," it said in a statement.
It said it expected financing to be set in time to allow the contract to get under way in the first quarter of 1997.
Bouygues also announced progress on a project in Beirut.
"A banking pool led by Paribas and Banque Indosuez has granted a French export credit of more than $100 million to the Solidere company," it said.
Solidere is a Lebanese firm which has awarded a sea-front design-and-build contract to Bouygues. Its share of the project amounts to around $120 million.
